newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's party chief slams decadent society.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's party chief slams decadent society.

text.p: Vietnam's Communist Party chief lashed out at the moral degeneration of society and corrupt and greedy officials in remarks published in the official party daily Nhan Dan on Thursday.

"At the present time, polarisation of wealth, moral degeneration and social evils have become serious within the party, within the state apparatus and within society," Secretary General Do Muoi was quoted as telling students at a Hanoi agricultural college.

Muoi drew a comparison with Vietnam's long history of dynastic rule, saying that kings and mandarins led dissipated lives while the people became poor after periods of peace and prosperity, leading to national decay and hostile invasions.

"...the people's strength must be applied to prevent, trample on and eliminate all of those negative things, making our regime stronger and stronger, protecting forever the fatherland's independence and unification," he was quoted as saying.
Muoi, who turns 80 in February, is viewed by western analysts as an ardent champion of socialist ideology and has several times this year spoken out against "hostile forces" and "peaceful evolution".

Both terms refer to concern that foreign influences and a loss of revolutionary fervour at home are whittling away at ideology, traditional national values and the party's grip on the fast-developing country.
Muoi was particularly critical of corruption and lashed out at officials who sought riches for themselves before trying to eliminate hunger and reduce poverty, the newspaper said.

"...If officials, party members and state officials are morally degenerate, thinking only of their own interests as opposed to the interests of the people, then the people will not trust them anymore," Nhan Dan quoted him as saying.
"We won in the war, but we would be defeated in peace."
